method: Compare prose excluded by both mechanical passes; inspect exact source clauses. This is not an independent semantic completeness review.

unclassifiedRows.text: This is an implementation task, not an audit, discussion, architecture exercise, or request for a downloadable patch.
The controlling disposition for every gate, stage determination, release determination, and terminal determination is evaluated in this exact order:
100% conformant to the tested deterministic invariants, with measured operational reliability of X.
For zero observed silent failures across N materially independent accepted operations, the approximate 95% upper bound 3/N may be reported.
The application remains a single, static, phone-first, provider-neutral, project-subject-neutral controller coordinating:
The controlling lifecycle has two valid commit paths.
No application-owned calculation is converted into a human-approved semantic proposal merely to fit a single lifecycle pattern.
This section resolves the central Stage 01 implementation failure.
Before Stage 01, the application possesses only raw human input and files the user has supplied.
There is no hidden pre-Stage-01 semantic intake agent.
Stage 01 is the first semantic extraction stage.
Files stored in browser-local application storage are not automatically present in an external AI conversation.
After the Stage 01 agent has inspected the request and supplied files, the accepted semantic intake becomes reusable canonical project information.
Read the complete request and every accessible supplied artifact from beginning to end. Extract all distinct project-relevant human-origin statements.
Raw coverage plus this mandatory semantic process provides enforceable accounting without falsely representing arbitrary semantic understanding as a deterministic application calculation.
Human confirmation is limited to genuine human-authority decisions.
Stage 02 inventories independent external sources that may govern, inform, or prove correctness.
A user-supplied project artifact is not automatically an independent external authority.
Stage 03 researches the accepted Stage 02 sources and extracts:
Stage 04 receives its complete input from the application.
Stage 04 is not allowed to rediscover an unspecified project from scratch.
Material-origin obligations derive from Stage 01's inspected supplied-material extraction and artifact provenance.
External-source obligations derive from Stage 03 research and candidate-requirement records.
For every obligation o in the application-generated input set:
One obligation may produce multiple atomic requirements.
Every original obligation identity remains independently traceable.
prompt-engine.js is the only prompt authority.
No runtime wrapper may modify prompt behavior after prompt-engine.js generates the exact string.

The prompt file does not contain its own bodySha256 or any value whose computation depends on bodySha256. manifest.json carries promptIdentity, including the application-computed bodySha256, and the prompt instructs the external actor to echo the exact manifest promptIdentity. This avoids a self-referential prompt hash.
When an external conversation requires a user message in addition to file attachment, prompt-engine.js generates this exact ASCII launcher and no other wrapper:
The following remain unchanged unless a demonstrated failing case requires a narrowly justified correction:
The Test IR requirement authorizes only the narrow additional runtime components needed for deterministic test execution.

The fixed external-handoff boundary is file-first: one authoritative prompt file, one manifest-bound input set, one authoritative response JSON file, and zero or more slot-bound returned files. Text previews and clipboard actions are not canonical transports.
test-worker.js is loaded only as the same-origin worker entry used by test-runtime.js.

workflow-schema.js owns the authoritative field registry, stage-operation registry, scope matrix, durable-object contracts, attachment-slot contract, verification-phase fields, and date/time value schemas.

test-runtime.js owns the Test IR language identity, operation-registry identity and digest, explicit DAG dataflow validation, parser and selector registry identities, and deterministic error propagation.

workflow-engine.js owns due-stage evaluation, release-state precedence, external-action risk evaluation, reservation state transitions, delivery-candidate closure, terminal prerequisite calculation, and the distinction between authorization, attempted delivery, and observed delivery.

project-store.js owns file-first prompt/response bytes, staging recovery, idempotency and tombstone receipts, backup/export state, logical handoff-container membership, quarantine handling, and exact original-byte preservation.

app-core.js renders untrusted values only through safe text and attribute APIs, applies the closed URL policy, exposes file-first actions, performs human confirmation without retyping, and presents actual-iPhone operator actions.
Repository CI owns the repository-only specification manifest and normative-requirement manifest. Those governance artifacts are not loaded into runtime project state or external project prompts.

The following versioned contract identities defined elsewhere in this specification are equally controlling and version-bound under Section 13.2: closed-loop-canonical-json/1, closed-loop-id/1, closed-loop-filename/1, closed-loop-handoff-container/1, closed-loop-specification-manifest/1, closed-loop-normative-requirements/1, closed-loop-deployment-manifest/1, closed-loop-encrypted-export/1, closed-loop-test-ir-language/1, closed-loop-test-ir-operations/1, closed-loop-json-selector/1, closed-loop-xml-selector/1, closed-loop-regex/1, closed-loop-trusted-time/1, closed-loop-raw-units/1, closed-loop-archive-profile/1 where archives are used, SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE_LIMITS/1, PROMPT_INLINE_LIMITS/1, and every parser, selector, regex, normalizer, and derivation registry identity.
union(all producer partitions) = complete field set
An unregistered field, multiply classified field, ambiguous producer, undeclared default, or operation writing outside its declared set is invalid.

Registry completeness is specification-controlled, not implementation-chosen. Every field named anywhere in this specification receives its complete FIELD_REGISTRY contract either from an explicit statement of this specification or from these closed default rules, applied in order:

The generated FIELD_REGISTRY, STAGE_OPERATION_REGISTRY, and normalizer and derivation registries are reviewed under the Section 2.2 omission-challenge discipline, and their digests are pinned in the Section 46.2 acceptance artifact.
Operation execution and response permissions are closed:

A human-origin fact or decision first supplied inside an external-agent conversation does not become HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION authority merely because the agent reports it. The response places each such value in humanAuthorityCandidates with its external-response pointer and claimed conversation basis. The application presents the exact extracted value for direct confirm or correct without requiring retyping. Information already present in current raw input or accepted human records is not reconfirmed.

Exact confirmation may be co-accepted atomically with the dependent agent proposal: the transaction creates the new human input or decision record first, revalidates that the response declared and used the identical confirmed value, binds the proposal to the confirmation receipt, and commits both or neither. This special co-acceptance does not permit any unconfirmed human value. A correction, omitted candidate, inconsistent value, or any other scope-changing input invalidates the response and requires a replacement prompt. This rule applies at every stage.

The renderer may show a combined view.
Every canonical record receives application-selected current-scope dimensions applicable to that record, including:
Every release-bearing proposition, proof obligation, test, observation obligation, regression, and deferred failure test declares:
promptIdentity.bodySha256 is the SHA-256 of the exact authoritative prompt-file bytes defined in Section 10.1.
promptIdentity.contractSha256 is the SHA-256 of the exact canonical current response contract.
promptIdentity.contextSignature is the SHA-256 of the exact canonical current scope and selected-context manifest.
promptIdentity.instructionId is application allocated under closed-loop-id/1.
No identity includes its own digest, the response bytes that later echo it, or another circularly dependent value.
Clarification, blockers, and execution failures are controlled response events. They are not accepted canonical data changes.
A duplicate-member ambiguity scan may run before JSON.parse. It is not a second semantic parser.
Phase 1 — file selection, staging, and raw capture
Reaccepting the same canonical envelope and scope returns existing identities and receipts and creates no duplicate state.
Every accepted agent value and relationship maps to:
Application-created IDs are recorded as application allocations, not falsely attributed to nonexistent response fields.

Every expected returned file has an application-owned ATTACHMENT_SLOT_ID bound to package, reservation, job, stage, operation, purpose, role, requiredness, allowed media type, filename rule, maximum size, and expected digest when known. The response attachment declaration references the slot ID and supplies claimed filename, media type, byte size, digest, and semantic role.

The permitted external time basis is governed by closed-loop-trusted-time/1. A VERIFIED_EXTERNAL time basis requires either a cryptographically verifiable external timestamp attestation, such as an RFC 3161 timestamp token, validated under a registered verification contract, or an attributable external-system record whose declared time authority the applicable proof obligation accepts. An unverified external time claim remains SOURCE_ASSERTED. Where neither basis exists, the obligation remains UNKNOWN.
humanInputRequests is the final structured fallback, not the normal conversation format.
An agent-provided filename or hash is a claim.
The application-computed SHA-256 of actual stored bytes is authority.

The UI and prompt identify the exact transfer action.

For every external stage or verification action, the application exports:

The current canonical handoff container is a logical manifest plus separately selected exact files. Its identity is the SHA-256 of the canonical manifest, which lists every member by package-relative canonical path, ATTACHMENT_SLOT_ID or outbound role, byte length, hash algorithm, digest, media type, disclosure classification, and requiredness. Member order, file-picker order, download order, and archive order are nonauthoritative.
The canonical manifest contains packageManifestSha256 computed from closed-loop-canonical-json/1 with packageManifestSha256 omitted. No package digest includes itself.

File extension and browser MIME type are claims. Format-dependent work records the authorized parser or adapter and detected interpretation. A materially ambiguous polyglot is BLOCKED unless one interpretation is explicitly authorized and every alternate interpretation is harmless under the operation.
The primary UI translates these modes into ordinary operator actions.
Technical enum values remain under advanced details.
An AI verification architect designs the test.
The application owns the test language, validates the test, and executes every faithfully expressible mechanical test.
The AI acts as a compiler targeting an application-owned declarative language.
The AI does not invent runtime semantics.

Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.
Any future "custom pipeline" may mean only a composition of registered declarative primitives.
Unknown or unsupported selector syntax fails Stage 06 ingestion.
Unsupported encodings route to an external executor or remain blocked.
Regex uses a restricted, safe, JavaScript-compatible subset with enforced limits.
PDF, DOCX, XLSX, SVG, DXF, STL, G-code, image, archive, and other specialized parsers are adapters.
Unsupported JSON Schema semantics route externally.
The implementation selects explicit constants, centralizes them, documents them, and regression-tests every boundary.
Every Test IR specification and every result binds:

Every canonical test declares VERIFICATION_PHASE, EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, REQUIRED_BY_STAGE, PER_RUN_REQUIRED, FINAL_PRODUCT_REQUIRED, DELIVERY_REQUIRED, and TARGET_AVAILABILITY_CONDITION. The application validates these values against the test role and proof obligation and derives when execution is due.
test-runtime.js is the single native Test IR authority.
workflow-engine.js queries this runtime and does not maintain a second executor registry.
Test execution occurs in a Web Worker.
Device time is not represented as trusted external time authority.
They use a dedicated validated application command.
The application validates and normalizes them into canonical application-owned results.
Producer authority does not change by route.
No second test interpreter or routing system may be created.
They are not agent-editable canonical fields.

Independent review can be generally routable at Stage 06. Actual context independence is established when the review is reserved and performed.
Every external, human, tool, system, physical, publication, filing, purchase, security, or production action is classified before package generation as one or more of:
READ_ONLY, REVERSIBLE, DESTRUCTIVE, IRREVERSIBLE, COST_INCURRING, THIRD_PARTY_AFFECTING, SECURITY_TESTING, PHYSICAL_HAZARD, or UNKNOWN.

Negative, adversarial, destructive, or security tests use isolated disposable state or an explicitly authorized bounded external sandbox. Canonical user projects and third-party systems are not mutation targets merely because a test requires an invalid state.

Every filesToSend and expectedReturnFiles entry has a stable application-owned slot or role ID. The UI and prompt use the same identifiers. The application exports the prompt and all send files directly from stored bytes and ingests the response and returned files through the corresponding slots.

Every canonical artifact with verified available bytes exposes an individual Download or Share action in the application. This retrieval requirement is distinct from the prohibition on returning an implementation patch instead of modifying the repository.

Returned files are selected into their named attachment slots. The application verifies actual bytes, membership, slot relationships, reservation, package, prompt identity, revision, scope, and response contract before proposal creation.
It does not call unobservable external separation application-proven.
Agent statements of independence are corroborating evidence only.
Blind aliases are not used when true identity is itself part of the requirement.
True RUN_ID is withheld unless the test requires it.
A warning not to use information is insufficient if the application embeds that information.
Requires explicit human-owned observation evidence recorded through the RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION command.
An AI claim that a human inspected something is insufficient.
Requires evidence attributable to the declared external system or capability.
When an artifact is evidence, the evidence record resolves to the canonical artifact.
Mentioning a filename in prose is insufficient.
Current readiness, release, or evidence-chain completeness becomes blocked or invalid if it depends on bytes that are no longer available and verified.
The shared evidence evaluator is consumed by:
Evidence rules are not reimplemented independently in every stage.

Every conditional activation proposition has either its own current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID or an explicitly identified activation leaf inside the parent applicability proof contract. It uses the same proof-expression, observation, entailment, evidence-class, allowed-epistemic-basis, freshness, contradiction, independence, and semantic-review rules as every other release-bearing proposition.

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.
It does not create another canonical collection.
Only current-scope records participate in current contradiction gating.
The contradiction evaluator remains defense in depth.
Current results concerning the same proposition establish incompatible conclusions.
Different propositions are not automatically contradictory.
A byte-hash success and a semantic-content violation are different propositions. The semantic violation still fails the product.
An adversarial violation is normally direct failure evidence, not automatically a contradiction.

The metadata store retains minimal nonproject command receipts necessary for idempotent DELETE_PROJECT and CLONE retries. A deletion tombstone contains only deleted JOB_ID, commandId, idempotency key, normalized payload hash, deletion result, committed metadata sequence, and retention expiry; it contains no substantive deleted project content. An exact retry returns the prior result.
No action silently converts quarantined data into current canonical state.

Each state records its actual evidence and epistemic basis. A package generated or duplicated inside the same IndexedDB origin is not an external backup; browser-local duplicate data in the same origin is not disaster-recovery backup evidence. Production maturity requires a successful restore from the exact exported package bytes.

A project hash or digest stored only with the data it describes establishes self-consistency and detectable corruption under the supported application. It does not authenticate against coordinated replacement by an actor that can change both bytes and stored digests, the browser, origin, application code, extension state, or device.

The UI labels this basis INTEGRITY_CHECKED. AUTHENTICATED requires an independently held expected digest, signature, MAC, trusted timestamp, or external checkpoint verified under a registered contract. The application may generate a one-action checkpoint containing project identity, revision, project digest, artifact-manifest digest, algorithms, contract profile, and device-reported time for external custody. The displayed evidence level remains the actual verified basis.

After an AUTHORIZED delivery record exists, the current Stage 30 operator action is EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS. It is a non-stage-increasing terminal action. Immediately before export or share, the application revalidates the current delivery record, dependency closure, recipient/destination scope, transfer-count rule, and exact artifact bytes.

It does not satisfy the current contract profile, file-first prompt and response transport, Stage 01 human-authority confirmation, Stage 02/03/04 challenge contracts, Test IR DAG and registry identities, worker identity, native Stage 22, due-stage logic, independence, evidence sufficiency, terminal delivery, actual-iPhone acceptance, visual preservation, or current live-path requirements.
Stage 01 is the first semantic intake stage.
No implementation may assume that the application already extracted arbitrary user-file meaning before the Stage 01 agent inspected the file.
After Stage 01 accepts the extracted human-authority information, no later stage may ask the user to supply that information again.
No human or agent assertion may substitute for a fact the application can establish itself.
No test, audit, source review, or deployment result substitutes for using the live application through the exact visible path.
Implementation-only instructions, repository audits, specification text, and repository governance manifests are not runtime project content and are not delegated to external stage agents.

Final delivery uses the exact Stage 25 delivery-candidate set, Stage 27 release precedence, Stage 28 byte identity and destination-bound human intent, Stage 29 evidence-chain hash, pre-delivery checkpoint, and the atomic Stage 30 terminal command. Authorization, delivery attempt, and completed delivery are distinct.

nextAction: Resolve remaining prose classifications and clause-specific production/evidence mapping; obtain genuinely independent semantic coverage review. Mechanical and continuation review are not independent semantic proof.
